title: Media processing corrupts creation timestamps and changes digest ordering

evidence.quote:
# Mark as processing
            item.status = "processing"
            # created_at doubles as processing start for stale-lock detection.
            item.created_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
            session.add(item)
            session.commit()

reasoning: _process_pending_items overwrites created_at to track processing start. That destroys the original item creation/discovery timestamp and directly affects later digest inclusion order, because completed media items are ordered by created_at when added to a digest. A retry or delayed processing can therefore reorder older media items and make client-visible created_at values inaccurate.
recommendation: Add or use a separate processing_started_at/updated_at field for stale-lock detection, leaving created_at immutable. Order digest media items by the intended stable timestamp.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests verify MediaItem.created_at remains stable after processing or that completed media items keep original ordering in digests.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create two pending MediaItems with distinct created_at values, process one later, and assert created_at is unchanged and digest selection order remains based on original creation time.
minimumFixScope: MediaItem processing timestamp handling and stale-lock query in media_pipeline.py.
